title: The King of Heaven His Table Spreads
description: The King of Heaven His Table Spreads in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 277 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “All Things Ready”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The King of heaven his ta-ble spreads, And dain-ties crown the board: Not Par-a-dise, with all its joys, Could such de-light af-ford.

lines: The King of heaven his table spreads,
Not Paradise, with all its joys,
Ye hungry poor, that long have strayed
Come from your most obscure retreats
And grace shall find you room.
Millions of souls, in glory now,
And millions more, still on the way,
Yet are his house and heart so large,
Nor could the whole assembled world

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
